text:
Marathon Petroleum has fallen 2.6% today and 8.3% over two weeks as refiners broadly face a shifting profit outlook. A major headline from Sunday captured the shift: analysts and headlines declared "the biggest money-making energy trade looks over," signaling that the exceptional refinery margins that drove the sector's rally are fading. With U.S. oil sitting at $89.53 per barrel and refineries running at 95.7% capacity, there's less room for the kind of outsized profits that made refiner stocks perform so well earlier in the cycle.

The broader geopolitical backdrop—Iran-backed attacks on Saudi and Bahraini facilities, U.S. sanctions tightening, and tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz—would normally support higher oil prices and refinery demand. Instead, those tailwinds appear insufficient to offset the market's recognition that the refining boom is cooling. The failed climate deal at COP31, which disappointed those hoping for stronger fossil fuel commitments, may also weigh on longer-term sentiment around energy infrastructure stocks.
